name: deck_generate
description: Make a deck from slides written in the JSON Narrato writes them in (`scaena generate --slides`, ADR-0026), with no model called: the spine, a section for each run of slides in one beat of the arc and a beat for each slide, each slide an absolute state in the theme layout its `layoutSuggestion` comes to, its builds, and the fields `deck_health` reads (`media.narrato`), lint's fixes applied. With `outline`, the big idea and each beat's claim the slides were written to, the sections are its beats and health holds the deck to its claims. A new bundle at `bundle`, in `theme`, as `deck_create` makes one; a deck in a script the theme's fonts do not draw is refused, since the CLI alone fetches a script's font.

GivenOutline.description: An outline written beside the slides (lift-up 10-25c FUNC-1).

bigIdea.description: The one sentence the audience should remember.

name.description: Its name ("Problem", "The ask"); `Beat N` without it.

claim.description: The one sentence its slides leave the audience believing. A beat with none is passed over.

slides.description: The slides it takes; spread from the length without it.

bundle.description: Where the bundle goes: a directory that is not there yet, or is empty.

slides.description:
The slides, as Narrato writes them: `executiveSummary`, and `slides`, each with
`slideTitle`, `subtitle`, `layoutSuggestion` (`Title`, `Bullet List`, `Big Number`,
`Chart`, `Two Column`, `Quote`, `Section Divider`, `Closing`, …), `keyBullets`,
`speakerNotes`, `beatIndex` and `beatName` (the arc's beat it belongs to), `intensity`
(0–1), `tone` (−1–1), and `visualDescription`; `chartData` where a chart is drawn.

theme.description:
The theme to make it in: one that ships, by name (`dusk`, `daybreak`, `ember`, `salon`),
or a theme file. `dusk` without it.

topic.description: What the deck is about, which health reads back; the executive summary without it.

audience.description: Who it is for ("Investors", "a school board").

length.description: `5-10 slides`, `11-15 slides`, `16-25 slides`, `26-40 slides`, or `41+ slides`.

language.description: The language the slides are written in, by its English name; English without it.

arc.description:
One of Narrato's arcs by name (`Problem-Solution`, `Hero's Journey`, …); without it,
chosen from the brief.

outline.description:
The big idea and each beat's claim the slides were written to, in the beats' order: the
deck's sections are its beats, a slide's `beatIndex` counting them from 0, and health
holds each slide to its beat's claim and the closing to the big idea.

voice.description: The voice its words take: tone, vocabulary, posture.

desiredOutcomes.description: What it should achieve, in the user's words.

persona.description: One of Narrato's personas, by its id, for an audience in the user's own words.

history.description: Keep a history, as `deck_create` does: on unless `false`.

created.description: Whether it was written: it is only if it validates.

files.description: Every file in it, by its path in the bundle.

Finding.description: One lint finding, shaped for agents: a code, a JSON pointer, and (when safe) a fix.

file.description: The bundle file `path` points into, when it is not `deck.json` (a theme file).

format.description: The format the deck was laid out in (`"9:16"`), when it is not the deck's own.

fix.description: A JSON Patch (RFC 6902) that resolves the finding. Only safe, non-content fixes.

refresh.description:
The data source to fetch again, where what resolves the finding is a fetch, which no patch
makes (W428, ADR-0030): the source's name, without its `@`.

fallback.description: Why the heuristic chose the arc, where none was named.

fixed.description: The findings whose fixes were applied, each checked by laying its state out again.
